texts: The film "Titanic" was actually filmed on location in several locations around the world, including New York City and Chicago. The shipwreck scene where the characters meet at sea is set in the harbor of New York Harbor, which is located in Lower Manhattan, New York City. The Titanic itself was also shot in various locations around the world, including on the banks of the Thames River in London, England; on the beaches of San Francisco, California; and on the shores of Lake Huron, Michigan. Additionally, scenes were shot in the Canadian city of Halifax, Nova Scotia, and on the island of Vancouver, British Columbia.

The film "Titanic," directed by James Cameron, had several filming locations around the world, including parts of it being shot in Canada. Specifically, scenes that required an icy, open sea setting were filmed off the coast of Newfoundland, Canada. The town of Halifax, Nova Scotia, was also used for some filming, particularly for scenes requiring a more urban backdrop.

One of the most notable Canadian locations used for the movie was CFB (Canadian Forces Base) Shearwater in Nova Scotia, which stood in for the docks where the Titanic would have departed. Additionally, parts of the movie were filmed on the MV Minia, a ship that was docked at Halifax Harbour and was used to represent the rescue ships involved in the aftermath of the Titanic's sinking.

These locations provided the necessary backdrop to create the historical and dramatic settings required for the film.

The film "Titanic" was filmed in various locations in Canada, but one of the most prominent sites was the scenic coast of Nova Scotia. The production team chose Halifax and the surrounding shoreline because of its striking resemblance to the icy North Atlantic waters where the historical event took place. Large sections of the ship were constructed on set in Halifax's expansive harbor, and the local shipyards provided the perfect backdrop for the grand ocean liner's scenes. Additionally, the crew utilized the frigid local waters to authentically capture the dramatic and tragic sinking sequences of the movie.

While many scenes in the 1997 film "Titanic" were shot on soundstages and utilized CGI, some exterior shots and the iconic prow scene were filmed in a large outdoor water tank at the Baja Studios in Rosarito, Mexico. There were no filming locations in Canada for this movie.
